Nigerian educators developed 'Schisto & Ladders,' a board game that teaches children how to prevent schistosomiasis, a parasitic disease common in impoverished areas.

The Poison:
The fact that such a simple, effective tool is needed highlights the systemic neglect of tropical diseases in impoverished regions.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
There is no plane error; the game aligns the WHAT (gameplay) with the WHY (prevention) perfectly.

Social Physics Analysis:
By integrating health education into a familiar game, the developers empowered the community to take ownership of their own health, minimizing external friction.

The Trajectory: The Path of Grace.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Grace. The solution is logically efficient and low-strain.

The Unavoidable Truth: Creative, low-cost solutions can have massive impacts on public health.

The Unavoidable Lie: Neglected tropical diseases are too complex to be addressed by simple community tools.
